summary: The finite-stage identities and strict pairwise gap estimates follow from the accepted all-double crossing and dominant inequalities, and their limiting weak forms are valid. The exact-cell sign convention correctly identifies each limiting c_i with the area of the corresponding positive normalized halfplane. With unit gradients and nonnegative constant affine dependence, both a two-weight limit and an all-positive collinear-gradient limit force a pair of positive halfplanes to cover the plane, contradicting the positive pairwise uncovered-area gap. Boundary cases and the single-positive-weight case are handled correctly.
